scenes.headline: How to steer a model's neurons in a tab
scenes.sub: Search a word, push a neuron, compare answers
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tarn! This page lets you pick one neuron inside a small language model, push it up or down, and read what changes. All of it runs in a browser tab.

scenes.text: Add a dose of one neuron's own direction to the model's state, then read three answers: pushed down, unchanged, and pushed up.
scenes.say: The idea is simple. Add a dose of one neuron's own direction to the model's state, then read three answers: pushed down, unchanged, and pushed up.

scenes.title: From a word to three answers

steps.say: Search a word. The lens lists which neurons make that word more or less likely.
Pick one. It writes a single fixed direction into the model's state.
Choose a dose. The engine runs the model right in your tab, with that push added.
Three versions decode together, so you can compare them side by side.

scenes.title: A model that runs in your browser

steps.say: The weights download once from Hugging Face and stay in your browser.
A worker runs the model in WebAssembly, with one hook that adds the dose to a neuron.
One pass over the weights per step feeds all three columns.

scenes.label: neurons passed every test for a bridge topic
scenes.say: Is a neuron a handle? In a search for a bridge topic, one neuron out of fifty eight thousand passed every test.

left.title: Qwen3-0.6B
items: Text gets worse as it works
left.say: On the small model I found one neuron, in a narrow window, and the text got worse as it worked.

right.title: Qwen3.5-4B recipe
right.say: The published recipe on the bigger model needed three neurons together. None of them worked alone.

scenes.text: A neuron is a handle only sometimes. Test it against random neurons, and compare pushed down, unchanged and pushed up.
